title: Hotfix: an unsigned image is blocked, and someone wants the policy off

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Binary Authorization: Key concepts
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: rule evaluation modes 'Allow all images', 'Disallow all images', 'Require attestations'; enforcement 'Block and Audit Log' versus 'Dry Run: Audit Log Only'; an attestation is a signed document over the image digest, verified by an attestor's public key; exempt images are always allowed via admissionWhitelistPatterns (patterns can match a whole registry path). The 'Use breakglass' page (read 2026-11-18): the Pod label image-policy.k8s.io/break-glass: 'true' is an 'emergency escape hatch that lets you override Binary Authorization policy enforcement', and 'a breakglass event is automatically logged to Cloud Audit Logs'; the denial message wording is an authored rendering.; the denial message wording is from memory.

brief.situation: You are the security engineer at Brisk Pay. A bug double-charges some card refunds; a developer built a one-line hotfix on a laptop, pushed it to Artifact Registry and tried to deploy it to the GKE cluster pay-prod. Binary Authorization denied it. The engineering lead asks you to 'turn the policy off for an hour'. The bank's refund batch runs at 15:00 and would hit the bug again.
handover: pay-prod's policy requires an attestation from attestor ci-verified, created by the CI pipeline after tests and a vulnerability scan pass.
The CI pipeline takes about 15 minutes end to end.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the cluster's Binary Authorization policy, the attestor, and the two ways the hotfix can reach production.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The bank's refund batch runs at 15:00, 55 minutes after the page.

writeup.question: For the record: why the deploy was denied, how you shipped the fix, and why the policy stayed on.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: No attestation from ci-verified existed: the image was built on a laptop and pushed directly. Its scan showed two critical vulnerabilities from a four-month-old base.

parts.label: Shipped
parts.modelAnswer: Pushed the branch and ran the pipeline: tests, scan and attestation in 14 minutes; deployed the attested digest before 15:00.

parts.label: Policy on
parts.modelAnswer: Allow-all would have run an unscanned image with critical vulnerabilities in the payments cluster. A logged breakglass procedure and a faster hotfix lane now cover real emergencies.

expertPath.text: Denied: no ci-verified attestation; policy requires it; laptop image has 2 critical CVEs; no CI run.
Push and run CI; deploy the attested digest; breakglass runbook, fast lane.
Attested digest running; test refund charged once.

gateOff.headline: The gate was the point
gateOff.body: Binary Authorization ensures only images that passed CI run in production. The fix was to send the hotfix through CI, not to remove the check.

doubleCharged.headline: Start the pipeline early
doubleCharged.body: A 15-minute pipeline fits in a 55-minute window if it starts at once.

attested.headline: Good: fast and still verified
attested.body: You read the denial and the policy, saw the laptop image would have shipped critical vulnerabilities, sent the fix through CI in time, verified the digest and a refund, and gave the team an audited emergency path.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The deploy was denied because the image has no attestation from the CI attestor: it was built on a laptop, and its scan shows critical vulnerabilities. Send the one-line fix through the pipeline, which tests, scans and attests in about 15 minutes, and deploy that digest well before 15:00. Allow-all would put an unscanned image into the payments cluster; retrying admits nothing. Give the team an audited breakglass path and a faster hotfix lane.
